samples.question: The picture shows two horizontal black rails, one above the other. The upper rail carries a row of black ticks pointing up; the lower rail carries a row of seven black ticks pointing down. Inside each row the ticks are evenly spaced, but the two rows do NOT use the same spacing, so the two rows drift in and out of step across the picture. Tick lengths vary from tick to tick and carry no information, and the pale grey marks in the gap between the two rails are decoration. For each lower tick measure the horizontal distance from it to the upper tick nearest to it; only horizontal position counts, never height, never vertical distance. Exactly one lower tick has a smaller such distance than every other lower tick: that is the tick that LINES UP. Number the lower ticks 1 to 7 from left to right. Which lower tick lines up? Answer with its number, 1 to 7.
